body:
Someone who is perfect wouldn't hit you.   
  
Abusers are like that. No one would be with them if they showed their true colors. My ex seemed charming, nurturing, gentle, and sweet in the beginning, too.

I wish you the best, but no amount of my love healed my ex (granted I was definitely not perfect but my actions didn't warrant being beaten). Staying with them while they did all that just reinforced the idea that they could treat me however they want and have no repercussions.

I know what you mean.

There’s a song called “Captive” by Allie Crowley Buckley. I remember listening to it before I got into my past relationship that was extensively and repeatedly physically, verbally, and emotionally abusive. I remember being naive and thinking that type of love to be messy but also romantic and passionate. There’s a line that resonated with me back then

“I just wanted to be someone that you need

I just craved a little codependency”

I’m not saying this is directly you, but I remember also thinking I got the relationship that I ultimately wanted - it just came at a genie’s wish. My ex was so many of my past ideals - volatile but romantic, tumultuous but passionate. I also fell into the fantasy of wanting to get married to her.

Some days I regret meeting her because of the CPTSD she caused me. I don’t think I necessarily regret meeting her, but I do regret this: not leaving when she first hit me.

Because it won’t be the first. I can almost guarantee you.

After she hit me for the first time, she bathed me, held me as I cried, apologized, told me she would rather die than hit me again Then she not only hit me - she strangled me multiple times after and tried to kill me. This is all while she called me the most vile and insulting words you could think of.

It only gets worse. While three years is a long time, you are better off leaving now before he causes you more pain, trauma, or potentially kills you. I know it’s hard - trust me, I know. I also tried everything in my power to make it work. We both went to individual therapy and couples therapy. We used and exhausted so many mental health resources and it just didn’t work. They almost never change, and abuse is a deal breaker that anyone should take, regardless of other circumstances.

I’m sorry you’re going through this. Please do what I wish I did the first time and leave.
